title: Bicep with Databases and Messaging
description: Deploy Azure SQL Database, Cosmos DB, Service Bus, and Event Grid using Bicep.

data.text: Data and messaging services are core parts of most applications. Bicep can deploy Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Service Bus queues and topics, and Event Grid topics alongside your application infrastructure.

data.title: Bicep - Azure SQL Database and Server
data.content: Deploy an Azure SQL server and database with firewall rules.

data.title: Bicep - Service Bus Namespace and Queue
data.content: Deploy a Service Bus namespace with a queue.

data.title: SQL Admin Password
data.text: Never hardcode the SQL admin password in a Bicep template. Use a secure parameter or retrieve it from Key Vault using the reference() function.

terms.definition: A fully managed relational database service. Deploy it as a server plus database pair in Bicep.
A globally distributed, multi-model database service. Supports SQL, MongoDB, Cassandra, Gremlin, and Table APIs.
A messaging primitive that stores messages until a consumer receives them. Supports at-least-once delivery and dead-letter queues.
An event routing service that delivers events from publishers to subscribers using a pub/sub model.

data.title: Common Data and Messaging Services in Bicep
items: Microsoft.Sql/servers and Microsoft.Sql/servers/databases for Azure SQL

data.title: Exercise: Deploy a Database and Queue
data.description: Create a Bicep template with an Azure SQL database and a Service Bus queue.
steps: Create a Bicep template with a SQL server parameter
Add a firewall rule to allow Azure services
Add a Service Bus namespace and queue
Output the SQL server name and Service Bus connection string
Deploy and verify both resources exist
data.expectedOutcome: A deployed Azure SQL database and Service Bus queue with connection details in the deployment outputs.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure SQL requires a server resource before creating databases
Service Bus uses namespace plus queue/topic resources
Use firewall rules to control SQL access
Output connection strings for use by application deployments
data.takeaway: Data and messaging services are first-class citizens in Bicep. Deploy them alongside your application infrastructure.
